"""SQLite connection and schema.

SQLite is the single store for this project: ~50 hubs x 10 years of daily weather
(~165k rows), FEMA NRI for all ~3.2k US counties, and Census place/county centroids.
"""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from app.config import get_settings

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hubs (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    region        TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    county_name   TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS daily_weather (
    hub_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES hubs(id),
    date           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- ISO date, local time of the hub
    tmax_c         REAL,
    tmin_c         REAL,
    precip_mm      REAL,
    snowfall_cm    REAL,
    wind_gust_kmh  REAL,
    weather_code   INTEGER,                -- WMO code (56/57/66/67 = freezing drizzle/rain)
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, date)
);

-- FEMA National Risk Index, one row per county x hazard, for ALL US counties.
-- freq_pctl (national percentile of annualized event frequency) is what scoring uses;
-- risk_score is kept for reference only (it scales with exposed property/population).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nri_county (
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard        TEXT NOT NULL,
    afreq         REAL,                    -- annualized frequency (events/year), NULL -> not applicable
    freq_pctl     REAL NOT NULL,           -- 0-100, national percentile of afreq (NULL treated as 0)
    alr_npctl     REAL,                    -- expected annual loss rate, national percentile
    risk_score    REAL,                    -- hazard type risk index score (exposure-driven)
    risk_rating   TEXT,
    nri_version   TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (county_fips, hazard)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS counties (
    county_fips   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS places (
    geoid         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa" (Census suffix like "city" removed)
    full_name     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa city"
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    aland_sqmi    REAL,                    -- land area; used to prefer the major place among same-name matches
    county_fips   TEXT                     -- nearest county centroid in the same state (approximation)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_places_name ON places(name);

-- NOAA HURDAT2 best tracks (Atlantic + NE Pacific), 6-hourly fixes, 1950+.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS storm_tracks (
    storm_id    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- e.g. AL092017
    name        TEXT,
    dt          TEXT NOT NULL,             -- ISO datetime (UTC)
    status      TEXT,                      -- TS, HU, SS, TD, EX, ...
    lat         REAL NOT NULL,
    lon         REAL NOT NULL,
    wind_kt     REAL,                      -- max sustained wind
    PRIMARY KEY (storm_id, dt)
);

-- NOAA SPC severe reports meeting the magnitude thresholds, kept only within the largest
-- tested radius of any hub (full national files stay cached in data/raw).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS severe_reports (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hazard      TEXT NOT NULL,             -- tornado | hail | wind
    date        TEXT NOT NULL,             -- local date of the report
    slat        REAL NOT NULL,
    slon        REAL NOT NULL,
    elat        REAL,                      -- tornado end point (NULL if unknown)
    elon        REAL,
    magnitude   REAL                       -- EF scale | hail inches | wind knots
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reports_hazard ON severe_reports(hazard, date);

-- Per-hub long-term event rates (Tier A), one row per hub x hazard x radius.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_event_rates (
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard          TEXT NOT NULL,         -- hurricane | hurricane_strength | tornado | hail | wind
    radius_km       REAL NOT NULL,
    first_year      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_year       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    events          INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- storms (hurricanes) or report days (convective)
    rate_per_year   REAL NOT NULL,
    rate_lo         REAL NOT NULL,         -- exact Poisson interval (confidence_level)
    rate_hi         REAL NOT NULL,
    p_horizon       REAL NOT NULL,         -- P(>= 1 event within horizon_years)
    horizon_years   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    params_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT,                  -- e.g. notable storms
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, hazard, radius_km)
);

-- Tier B: the GHCN-Daily station chosen for each hub by the fixed selection rule.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_stations (
    hub_id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    station_name    TEXT,
    lat             REAL, lon REAL,
    distance_km     REAL NOT NULL,
    completeness_json TEXT NOT NULL,       -- per element share of days present, 1996-2025
    candidates_tried INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS station_daily (
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    date            TEXT NOT NULL,
    prcp_mm         REAL,
    snow_cm         REAL,                  -- measured snowfall
    tmax_c          REAL,
    tmin_c          REAL,
    gust_kmh        REAL,                  -- WSF5: fastest 5-second wind
    wt_thunder      INTEGER,               -- WT03 observed (1) / not recorded (0)
    wt_ice_pellets  INTEGER,               -- WT04
    wt_hail         INTEGER,               -- WT05
    wt_glaze        INTEGER,               -- WT06
    wt_freezing_rain INTEGER,              -- WT17
    PRIMARY KEY (station_id, date)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_metrics (
    hub_id        TEXT NOT NULL,
    metric        TEXT NOT NULL,
    period        TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "2016-2025" or "2025"
    value         REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, metric, period)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS risk_scores (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    computed_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
    scoring_version TEXT NOT NULL,
    composite       REAL NOT NULL,
    winter          REAL, hurricane REAL, flood REAL, convective REAL, heat REAL,
    tier            TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scores_hub ON risk_scores(hub_id, computed_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
    old_value   REAL,
    new_value   REAL,
    message     TEXT NOT NULL,
    delivered   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ingest_log (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    source      TEXT NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    params      TEXT,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL,
    rows        INTEGER,
    note        TEXT
);
"""


def get_connection(db_file: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = db_file or get_settings().db_file
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn


def create_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    conn.commit()

"""

from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import create_schema, get_connection
from app.ingest import census_gazetteer, fema_nri, hubs, open_meteo


def summarize(conn) -> None:
    q = lambda sql: conn.execute(sql).fetchone()[0]  # noqa: E731
    print("\nDatabase summary")
    print(f"  hubs:           {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hubs')}")
    print(f"  daily_weather:  {q('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM daily_weather')} rows, "
          f"{q('SELECT MIN(date) FROM daily_weather')} .. {q('SELECT MAX(date) FROM daily_weather')}")

    ).fetchall()
    missing_nri = conn.execute(
        "SELECT h.id FROM hubs h LEFT JOIN nri_county n ON n.county_fips = h.county_fips "
        "GROUP BY h.id HAVING COUNT(n.hazard) = 0"

    if missing_nri:

def main() -> None:

        print(f"  {open_meteo.ingest(conn, hub_list, refresh=args.refresh)}")

    summarize(conn)
    conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Long-term event rates around each hub (Tier A), for every configured radius.

Hurricanes (HURDAT2, 1950+): a storm counts if its track (densified between 6-hourly
fixes) passes within the radius while at tropical-storm strength or more. Storms that
were at hurricane strength at that point are counted separately.

Convective (SPC, 1996+): counted as report days, i.e. distinct dates with at least one
qualifying report within the radius (tornado distance is measured to the path segment).

Each rate gets an exact Poisson interval and P(at least one event in the horizon).

Usage:
    python -m app.scoring.event_rates          # compute and store
    python -m app.scoring.event_rates --test   # also print the radius test and FEMA cross-check
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import sqlite3

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import chi2, spearmanr

from app.db import get_connection
from app.geo import haversine_km, point_to_segment_km
from app.scoring.params import get_params


def poisson_interval(k: int, years: int, level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    a = 1 - level
    lo = 0.0 if k == 0 else chi2.ppf(a / 2, 2 * k) / 2
    hi = chi2.ppf(1 - a / 2, 2 * k + 2) / 2
    return lo / years, hi / years


def densify_tracks(conn: sqlite3.Connection, step_km: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Linearly interpolate each storm's track so consecutive points are <= step_km apart."""
    t = pd.read_sql("SELECT storm_id, name, dt, status, lat, lon, wind_kt FROM storm_tracks ORDER BY storm_id, dt", conn)
    out = []
    for sid, g in t.groupby("storm_id", sort=False):
        lat, lon, wind, status = g["lat"].to_numpy(), g["lon"].to_numpy(), g["wind_kt"].to_numpy(), g["status"].to_numpy()
        for i in range(len(g)):
            out.append((sid, lat[i], lon[i], wind[i], status[i]))
            if i + 1 < len(g):
                d = float(haversine_km(lat[i], lon[i], lat[i + 1], lon[i + 1]))
                n = int(d // step_km)
                for j in range(1, n + 1):
                    f = j / (n + 1)
                    w = None if (wind[i] is None or wind[i + 1] is None or np.isnan(wind[i]) or np.isnan(wind[i + 1])) \
                        else wind[i] + f * (wind[i + 1] - wind[i])
                    out.append((sid, lat[i] + f * (lat[i + 1] - lat[i]), lon[i] + f * (lon[i + 1] - lon[i]), w, status[i]))
    pts = pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["storm_id", "lat", "lon", "wind_kt", "status"])
    names = t.drop_duplicates("storm_id").set_index("storm_id")["name"]
    pts["name"] = pts["storm_id"].map(names)
    return pts


def hurricane_rates(conn, hubs, p) -> list[dict]:
    hp = p["hurricane"]
    years = hp["last_year"] - hp["first_year"] + 1
    pts = densify_tracks(conn, hp["interpolate_step_km"])
    pts = pts[pts["storm_id"].str[-4:].astype(int).between(hp["first_year"], hp["last_year"])]
    wind = pts["wind_kt"].fillna(0).to_numpy()
    eligible = pts["status"].isin(hp["statuses"]).to_numpy() & (wind >= hp["min_wind_kt"])
    hurricane = (pts["status"] == "HU").to_numpy() & (wind >= hp["hurricane_wind_kt"])
    rows = []
    for hub_id, lat, lon in hubs:
        d = haversine_km(lat, lon, pts["lat"].to_numpy(), pts["lon"].to_numpy())
        for r in p["radii_km"]["hurricane"]:
            near = d <= r
            for hazard, mask in (("hurricane", near & eligible), ("hurricane_strength", near & hurricane)):
                sel = pts[mask].assign(dist=d[mask])
                storms = sel.groupby("storm_id").agg(name=("name", "first"), max_wind_kt=("wind_kt", "max"),
                                                    closest_km=("dist", "min"))
                notable = storms.sort_values("max_wind_kt", ascending=False).head(8)
                notable_list = [
                    {"storm": f"{row.name.title()} {sid[-4:]}", "max_wind_kt_nearby": None if pd.isna(row.max_wind_kt) else int(row.max_wind_kt),
                     "closest_km": round(float(row.closest_km))}
                    for sid, row in notable.iterrows()
                ]
                rows.append(_rate_row(hub_id, hazard, r, hp["first_year"], hp["last_year"], len(storms), years, p,
                                      {"notable_storms": notable_list}))
    return rows


def convective_rates(conn, hubs, p) -> list[dict]:
    cp = p["convective"]
    years = cp["last_year"] - cp["first_year"] + 1
    rep = pd.read_sql("SELECT hazard, date, slat, slon, elat, elon, magnitude FROM severe_reports", conn)
    rows = []
    for hazard in ("tornado", "hail", "wind"):
        h = rep[rep["hazard"] == hazard]
        for hub_id, lat, lon in hubs:
            d = point_to_segment_km(lat, lon, h["slat"], h["slon"], h["elat"], h["elon"])
            for r in p["radii_km"]["convective"]:
                days = h.loc[d <= r, "date"].nunique()
                rows.append(_rate_row(hub_id, hazard, r, cp["first_year"], cp["last_year"], int(days), years, p,
                                      {"unit": "report days"}))
    return rows


def _rate_row(hub_id, hazard, radius, y0, y1, k, years, p, details) -> dict:
    lo, hi = poisson_interval(k, years, p["confidence_level"])
    rate = k / years
    h = p["probability_horizon_years"]
    return {"hub_id": hub_id, "hazard": hazard, "radius_km": radius, "first_year": y0, "last_year": y1,
            "events": k, "rate_per_year": rate, "rate_lo": lo, "rate_hi": hi,
            "p_horizon": 1 - math.exp(-rate * h), "horizon_years": h,
            "params_version": get_params()["params_version"], "details_json": json.dumps(details)}


def compute(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
    p = get_params()["event_rates"]
    hubs = conn.execute("SELECT id, lat, lon FROM hubs ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    rows = hurricane_rates(conn, hubs, p) + convective_rates(conn, hubs, p)
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM hub_event_rates")
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT INTO hub_event_rates VALUES (:hub_id, :hazard, :radius_km, :first_year, :last_year, :events, "
        ":rate_per_year, :rate_lo, :rate_hi, :p_horizon, :horizon_years, :params_version, :details_json)", rows)
    conn.commit()
    return {"rows": len(rows)}


def radius_test(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    """Rank stability of hubs across radii (Spearman), plus a cross-check against FEMA."""
    p = get_params()["event_rates"]
    df = pd.read_sql("SELECT hub_id, hazard, radius_km, rate_per_year FROM hub_event_rates", conn)
    print("\nRadius test: Spearman rank correlation of hub rates between radii")
    for hazard, kind in (("hurricane", "hurricane"), ("hurricane_strength", "hurricane"),
                         ("tornado", "convective"), ("hail", "convective"), ("wind", "convective")):
        piv = df[df["hazard"] == hazard].pivot(index="hub_id", columns="radius_km", values="rate_per_year")
        radii = p["radii_km"][kind]
        pairs = [(radii[i], radii[i + 1]) for i in range(len(radii) - 1)] + [(radii[0], radii[-1])]
        txt = ", ".join(f"{a:g}-{b:g} km: {spearmanr(piv[a], piv[b]).statistic:.2f}" for a, b in pairs)
        print(f"  {hazard:<19} {txt}")

    fema = pd.read_sql(
        "SELECT h.id hub_id, n.hazard, n.afreq FROM hubs h JOIN nri_county n ON n.county_fips = h.county_fips", conn)
    print("\nCross-check vs FEMA NRI annualized frequency (hub counties), Spearman at default radius")
    for ours, theirs, kind in (("tornado", "tornado", "convective"), ("hail", "hail", "convective"),
                               ("wind", "strong_wind", "convective"), ("hurricane", "hurricane", "hurricane")):
        r = p["default_radius_km"][kind]
        a = df[(df.hazard == ours) & (df.radius_km == r)].set_index("hub_id")["rate_per_year"]
        b = fema[fema.hazard == theirs].set_index("hub_id")["afreq"].fillna(0)
        print(f"  {ours:<10} vs FEMA {theirs:<12} rho = {spearmanr(a, b.reindex(a.index)).statistic:.2f}")


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--test", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    conn = get_connection()
    print(compute(conn))
    if args.test:
        radius_test(conn)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""NOAA GHCN-Daily station observations for each hub (Tier B).

Station rule (params.yaml -> stations): nearest USW (first-order, usually a major airport)
station within max_distance_km whose records for required_elements are at least
min_completeness complete over first_year..last_year. Candidates come from NOAA's station
inventory; completeness is checked on the downloaded data, and the next-nearest candidate
is tried if a station falls short. Data come from the NCEI Access Data Service (no token).
"""

import io
import json
import sqlite3
import time

import pandas as pd

from app.config import get_settings
from app.geo import haversine_km
from app.ingest.common import get_with_retry, http_client, log_ingest
from app.scoring.params import get_params

WT_COLUMNS = {"WT03": "wt_thunder", "WT04": "wt_ice_pellets", "WT05": "wt_hail",
              "WT06": "wt_glaze", "WT17": "wt_freezing_rain"}


def _cached_text(url: str, name: str, refresh: bool) -> str:
    path = get_settings().raw_dir / "ghcn" / name
    if refresh or not path.exists():
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with http_client(timeout=300) as c:
            path.write_bytes(get_with_retry(c, url).content)
    return path.read_text(encoding="latin-1")


def load_candidates(refresh: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """USW stations whose inventory covers the window for all required elements."""
    sp = get_params()["stations"]
    rows = []
    for line in _cached_text(sp["stations_url"], "ghcnd-stations.txt", refresh).splitlines():
        sid = line[0:11]
        if sid[2:5] != sp["station_prefix"]:
            continue
        rows.append({"station_id": sid, "lat": float(line[12:20]), "lon": float(line[21:30]),
                     "name": line[41:71].strip()})
    stations = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    inv = pd.read_fwf(
        io.StringIO(_cached_text(sp["inventory_url"], "ghcnd-inventory.txt", refresh)),
        colspecs=[(0, 11), (31, 35), (36, 40), (41, 45)], names=["station_id", "element", "first", "last"],
    )
    inv = inv[inv["station_id"].str[2:5] == sp["station_prefix"]]
    ok = None
    for el in sp["required_elements"]:
        covers = inv[(inv["element"] == el) & (inv["first"] <= sp["first_year"]) & (inv["last"] >= sp["last_year"])]
        ids = set(covers["station_id"])
        ok = ids if ok is None else ok & ids
    return stations[stations["station_id"].isin(ok)].reset_index(drop=True)


def fetch_station(station_id: str, refresh: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sp = get_settings()
    p = get_params()["stations"]
    cache = sp.raw_dir / "ghcn" / "daily" / f"{station_id}.csv"
    if refresh or not cache.exists():
        cache.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        params = {
            "dataset": "daily-summaries", "stations": station_id,
            "startDate": f"{p['first_year']}-01-01", "endDate": f"{p['last_year']}-12-31",
            "dataTypes": ",".join(p["elements"]), "format": "csv", "units": "metric",
            "includeAttributes": "false",
        }
        with http_client(timeout=300) as c:
            cache.write_bytes(get_with_retry(c, p["data_url"], params).content)
        time.sleep(1)
    return pd.read_csv(cache, dtype={"STATION": str})


def completeness(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    p = get_params()["stations"]
    days = len(pd.date_range(f"{p['first_year']}-01-01", f"{p['last_year']}-12-31"))
    out = {}
    for el in ("PRCP", "SNOW", "TMAX", "TMIN", "WSF5"):
        out[el] = round(float(df[el].notna().sum()) / days, 4) if el in df.columns else 0.0
    out["any_WT"] = round(float(df[[c for c in WT_COLUMNS if c in df.columns]].notna().any(axis=1).sum()) / days, 4) \
        if any(c in df.columns for c in WT_COLUMNS) else 0.0
    return out


def to_rows(station_id: str, df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[tuple]:
    def col(name):
        return df[name] if name in df.columns else pd.Series([None] * len(df))

    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "station_id": station_id,
        "date": df["DATE"],
        "prcp_mm": col("PRCP"),
        "snow_cm": col("SNOW") / 10.0 if "SNOW" in df.columns else None,   # service returns mm
        "tmax_c": col("TMAX"),
        "tmin_c": col("TMIN"),
        "gust_kmh": col("WSF5") * 3.6 if "WSF5" in df.columns else None,   # m/s -> km/h
    })
    for wt, name in WT_COLUMNS.items():
        out[name] = col(wt).notna().astype(int) if wt in df.columns else 0
    return [tuple(None if pd.isna(v) else v for v in r) for r in out.itertuples(index=False)]


def ingest(conn: sqlite3.Connection, refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
    p = get_params()["stations"]
    cands = load_candidates(refresh)
    hubs = conn.execute("SELECT id, lat, lon FROM hubs ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM hub_stations")
    chosen, problems = {}, []
    for hub_id, lat, lon in hubs:
        d = cands.assign(distance_km=haversine_km(lat, lon, cands["lat"], cands["lon"]))
        d = d[d["distance_km"] <= p["max_distance_km"]].sort_values("distance_km")
        picked = None
        for tried, st in enumerate(d.itertuples(), 1):
            df = fetch_station(st.station_id, refresh)
            comp = completeness(df)
            if all(comp[el] >= p["min_completeness"] for el in p["required_elements"]):
                picked = (st, df, comp, tried)
                break
        if picked is None:
            problems.append(hub_id)
            continue
        st, df, comp, tried = picked
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM station_daily WHERE station_id = ?", (st.station_id,))
        conn.executemany(
            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO station_daily VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", to_rows(st.station_id, df))
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO hub_stations VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                     (hub_id, st.station_id, st.name, st.lat, st.lon, round(float(st.distance_km), 1),
                      json.dumps(comp), tried))
        conn.commit()
        chosen[hub_id] = st.station_id
        print(f"  {hub_id}: {st.station_id} {st.name} ({st.distance_km:.1f} km) {comp}")
    log_ingest(conn, "ghcn_daily", "ok" if not problems else "partial", rows=len(chosen),
               params={k: p[k] for k in ("max_distance_km", "first_year", "last_year", "min_completeness")},
               note=f"no qualifying station: {problems}" if problems else None)
    return {"hubs_with_station": len(chosen), "no_station": problems}

content.text:
Most of the remaining work doesn't need the downloads to finish. Only the final scoring *results* and end-to-end agent tests need the complete data. Here's what can run in parallel, best first:

**1. Phase 3 scoring code, tested on synthetic data** *(best next step)*
- Write the metric functions (snow days, ice days, heavy-rain days and so on), with each day's value taken from the station when present and from Open-Meteo otherwise, and the source recorded.
- Write the scoring engine (sub-scores, composite, tiers, breakdown) and its unit tests on small made-up data.
- **This also follows our parameter rule:** thresholds, weights and the normalization method get fixed in `params.yaml` *before* we see any real rankings. Waiting for the data and then choosing would be exactly the confirmation-bias risk you raised.
- When the downloads finish, we run it once and review the results.

**2. `find_nearest_hubs`, the stand-in feature**
- Its data is already complete: places, counties, FEMA data for every county, and hub coordinates.
- It can be built and fully tested now (Tampa, Spokane, Springfield, the aliases).

**3. Agent infrastructure (Phases 4–6):** the tool schemas, the OpenAI client, the answer schema, the validator, the agent loop and the API. None of it depends on the final numbers. It just needs a database to read, and a partial one works for development.

**4. A Phase 2 checkpoint commit (code only):** the ingestion code is done, so committing it now protects the work. The database itself gets committed once it's complete.

**The one thing to avoid:** another job that *writes* to the database at the same time. Reading is fine.

My suggested order: **commit (4) → scoring code (1) → stand-in tool (2)**. By then the downloads should be done, and we run the scoring on real data.

content.text:
Phase 2 code is committed as `7ccbc22` and pushed to [GitHub](https://github.com/omrikantor/weather-risk-agent). That's 17 files: the ingestion modules, `params.yaml` and the hub list with county codes. **The database is left out on purpose** until the station and weather downloads finish.

Below is exactly what's needed for parts 1 and 2. Under our parameter rule, the choices marked 🔒 get fixed **before** we see any real rankings, so I need your approval on those first.

---

# Part 1: Phase 3, the scoring code (≈2.5–3 h)

### Step 1.1: Combine each day's data from both sources (`app/scoring/metrics.py`)
- For each hub, day and variable (1996–2025): **use the station value if it exists, otherwise Open-Meteo** (which only covers 2016–2025). Record which source each value came from.
- Days with no data from either source are **left out of the calculation**, not counted as zero.
- **Annual counts are adjusted for missing days:** count ÷ days with data × 365.25. For example, if a station has data on only 300 days of a year and recorded 6 snow days, that becomes about 7.3 snow days per year.
- 🔒 **Minimum coverage 80%:** if a hub has data for less than 80% of days for some variable, use Open-Meteo's 2016–2025 data for that variable instead, and lower the hub's confidence level.

### Step 1.2: Define the metrics 🔒
| Metric | Definition | Reason | Change from the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Snow day | ≥ 1 cm measured | Common "measurable snow" level | — |
| Heavy snow day | ≥ 10 cm | Clearly disruptive | — |
| **Ice day** | Station recorded glaze, freezing rain or ice pellets | Observed, not estimated | Replaces the temperature proxy |
| Extreme cold day | Low ≤ −15 °C | Same as the plan | — |
| Heavy rain day | ≥ 50 mm (~2 in) | Common flash-flood level | — |
| Wettest 3 days | Each year's largest 3-day total, averaged | Captures multi-day storms | — |
| **Damaging gust day** | Measured gust ≥ **93 km/h** (58 mph) | The same severe-wind threshold used to filter the SPC reports, so the two are consistent | Was 80 km/h |
| Extreme heat day | High ≥ 38 °C (100 °F) | — | — |
| Thunder day | Station recorded thunder | **Shown for information, not scored**, because stations record it inconsistently | New |
| **Disruption day** (second KPI) | Any of: snow ≥ 5 cm, an ice day, gust ≥ 93 km/h, rain ≥ 50 mm, high ≥ 38 °C | A day likely to disrupt operations | Heat threshold aligned to 38 °C |

All metrics are also stored **per year**, so "last year" questions work.

### Step 1.3: Put each input on a 0–100 scale 🔒 (the most important choice)
| Option | Problem |
|---|---|
| Percentile rank among hubs | Squashes big differences (Phoenix's hurricane "50") |
| Scale against the maximum | A single extreme hub squashes all the others |
| **Scale against the 95th-percentile hub, capped at 100** ✅ | Keeps real size differences (0 means none) without letting one outlier distort everything |

**Formula:** score = 100 × value ÷ (the value at the 95th percentile among hubs), capped at 100.

The same method applies to **every input**, ours and FEMA's (instead of FEMA's national percentiles), so all inputs are scaled consistently.

### Step 1.4: Hazard scores 🔒
Within each hazard, the inputs carry **equal weight unless there's a stated reason**:

| Hazard | Inputs | Weighting |
|---|---|---|
| **Winter** | Snow days, heavy snow days, ice days, extreme cold days *(stations)* + FEMA winter weather, ice storm, cold wave | 50% station data / 50% FEMA |
| **Hurricane** | Tropical-storm rate within 150 km + hurricane-strength rate (1950–2025) | 50 / 50 |
| **Flood** | Heavy rain days, wettest 3 days + FEMA inland flood, coastal flood | 50 / 50 |
| **Convective** | Tornado, hail and wind report days (SPC, 50 km) + measured damaging-gust days | 25% each |
| **Heat** | Extreme heat days + FEMA heat wave | 50 / 50 |

### Step 1.5: The overall risk index and tiers 🔒
- **Composite weights:** winter .25, flood .20, hurricane .20, convective .20, heat .15. These are unchanged from the plan. Heat is lowest because it rarely closes a hub outright.
- **Tiers:** the top third of hubs is **High**, the middle third **Elevated** and the bottom third **Low**. The scores are relative to our network, so fixed cutoffs like "≥ 60" wouldn't mean anything.
- **Confidence per hub** (high / medium / low), set by fixed rules: station distance (> 25 km lowers it), the share of days filled from Open-Meteo, and how many events stand behind the rare-event rates.

### Step 1.6: Outputs
- **`hub_metrics`:** every metric for each hub and period, with units, data coverage and sources.
- **`risk_scores`:** a new row for each run, tagged with the parameter version, so the alert feature can compare runs.
- **`breakdown(hub)`:** each hazard's contribution to the overall score, each input's contribution within its hazard, the raw values, uncertainty ranges and notable storms. This answers *"Why is Dallas high?"*
- **Command:** `python -m app.scoring.engine --print` shows the ranking. It's also added as a `score` step in `build_db`.

### Step 1.7: Unit tests on made-up data (no real data needed)
- Thresholds count correctly.
- Missing days are adjusted for correctly.
- The station value is preferred, with Open-Meteo as the fallback.
- Scaling: 0 stays 0, and values are capped at 100.
- Weights sum to 1 within each hazard and in the overall index.
- Breakdown contributions add up exactly to the overall score.
- Tiers split the hubs into thirds.
- The same input always gives the same output.

### Step 1.8: Run on real data (after the downloads)
Print the rankings and check for **bugs only**: unexpected rankings are findings, not something to adjust. Record the findings, then commit.

---

# Part 2: `find_nearest_hubs`, the stand-in tool (≈1 h, all data ready)

### Step 2.1: Clean up the input
- Accept forms like "Tampa", "Tampa, FL", "tampa florida" or "St. Petersburg".
- Ignore case and punctuation; treat "St." and "Saint" the same; convert state names to two-letter codes.

### Step 2.2: Find the place, trying these in order
1. Is it one of our hubs? Then report that we have data for it.
2. Exact name match, plus state if given.
3. Aliases, generated by rule: "Boise City" → Boise, "Urban Honolulu" → Honolulu, "Nashville-Davidson" → Nashville.
4. Match on the start of the name.
5. Typo tolerance, using Python's built-in close-match tool with a strict cutoff (0.85).
6. Nothing matched → report it as **not found**.

**Several matches and no state given** 🔒: if the largest match is at least **10 times** the land area of the next one, pick it (Tampa, FL at 114 sq mi vs Tampa, KS at 0.18). Otherwise return the top 5 candidates as **ambiguous**, and the agent asks which one was meant (Springfield).

### Step 2.3: Find the 3 nearest hubs
Straight-line distance from the place to all 47 hubs.

### Step 2.4: Compare hazard profiles 🔒
- The place's county and each candidate hub's county each get **10 FEMA hazard frequencies**, scaled exactly as in Step 1.3 for consistency.
- **Similarity = 100 × (1 − the average difference between the two profiles)**. Easy to explain: "on average, the profiles differ by X%."
- **The 2 largest differences** are reported with their direction, e.g. *"Miami has much higher hurricane frequency."*

### Step 2.5: Recommend a stand-in 🔒
- **Recommendation score = 0.8 × similarity + 0.2 × proximity**, where proximity runs from 100 at 0 km down to 0 at 500 km.
- **If the recommended hub is more than 250 km away,** a "far away" caveat is added.
- All of these values go into `params.yaml`.

### Step 2.6: Output format
A fixed, typed structure:
- the status (`is_hub` / `matched` / `ambiguous` / `not_found`);
- the place found, with its approximate county;
- the 3 candidates, each with distance, similarity, proximity, combined score and largest differences;
- the recommended hub, the caveats, and a one-line description of the method.

The code lives in `app/tools/locate.py` as a plain function; Phase 4 wraps it as an agent tool.

### Step 2.7: Tests
They check that everything behaves consistently, not that specific cities "look right":

| Query | Expected |
|---|---|
| Tampa | Florida (matched) |
| Springfield | `ambiguous` |
| Dallas | `is_hub` |
| Boise | `is_hub` (via the alias) |
| Spokane | the far-away caveat |
| Honolulu | matched, with the far-away caveat |
| "Tampaa" | Tampa (typo handled) |
| "Xyzville" | `not_found` |

The tests also check that the candidates really are the 3 nearest, sorted by distance, that similarity stays between 0 and 100, and that results are identical on repeated runs.

---

| # | Choice | Proposed |

| 1 | Minimum data coverage | 80%; below that, fall back to Open-Meteo |
| 2 | Damaging-gust threshold | 93 km/h (matches the SPC filter) |
| 3 | Thunder days | Shown for information only, not scored |
| 4 | Scaling method | Against the 95th-percentile hub, capped at 100, for all inputs |
| 5 | Weights within each hazard | Equal (50/50 between station and FEMA) |
| 6 | Composite weights | .25 / .20 / .20 / .20 / .15 |
| 7 | Tiers | Thirds of the network |
| 8 | Ambiguous names | Pick a place only if it's ≥ 10× larger in land area, otherwise ask |
| 9 | Stand-in scoring | 0.8 similarity + 0.2 proximity (zero at 500 km); caveat beyond 250 km |

content.text:
## 1. The station fix (choice #10)

**What WSF5 is:** the fastest 5-second wind gust of the day. It's measured by the automated weather stations (ASOS) at major airports, which carry the full set of instruments: wind sensor, precipitation, temperature and weather-event detection.

**Why the current rule picks the wrong stations:** it says *"take the nearest `USW` station with ≥ 90% complete precipitation and temperature."* `USW` also includes **secondary stations**: an old airport (Denver-Stapleton, closed in 1995 but still recording temperature and rain), a park (New Orleans Audubon), a downtown rooftop site (San Francisco). They pass the precipitation and temperature check because they record those two, but they have **no wind sensor**, and usually don't report weather events either. Since they're closer to the city center, the rule chooses them.

**What the fix changes:** add gusts to the required list, so the rule becomes *"the nearest station with ≥ 90% complete precipitation, temperature **and** gusts."* Requiring gusts works as a test for "has the full instrument set," which in practice means the main airport station.

**Why gusts and not the weather events:** event flags only appear on days when something happens (thunder, ice), so their completeness can't be measured. Gusts are recorded every day, so they're a reliable test.

**Trade-off:** the chosen station may be a bit farther away. For example, Denver International is roughly 30 km from downtown versus 11 km for Stapleton.

**Fallback, so the rule always works:** if no station within 40 km has gust data, take the nearest station with precipitation and temperature and **mark that hub as having no measured gusts**. That lowers the hub's confidence level and uses Open-Meteo for gusts.

**One correction:** I named DEN, MSY, OAK, SMF and SEA as the likely results, but **I haven't checked that yet**. The rule decides, and we'll see the actual choices when it runs.

## 2. The composite weights
To be direct: **.25 / .20 / .20 / .20 / .15 was my judgment, not something derived from data.** My reasons were that winter disruption is frequent across many hubs and heat rarely closes a hub. But I didn't test that, and it's exactly the kind of prior knowledge you asked me not to build in.

**Better approach:**
1. **Equal weights (0.2 each) as the default.** With no business data on which hazard costs this company the most, equal weights are the choice that assumes the least, and they're the easiest to defend: "no hazard is assumed to matter more than another."
2. **Weight sensitivity test,** like the radius test: rank the hubs under several alternative weightings (e.g. each hazard doubled in turn) and report how stable the top and bottom of the ranking are. If they're stable, the weights matter little; if not, the agent says the ranking depends on the weighting.
3. **Analysts can set their own weights** through a tool parameter, e.g. *"rank with hurricanes weighted double."* It stays deterministic, because the weights are explicit inputs and are shown in the answer.
4. **Disruption days per year,** the second KPI, uses no weights at all, so it acts as a weight-free check on the index.

In a real engagement the weights would come from the client's own disruption-cost data. The design doc will say so.

## 3. The 10× rule for ambiguous names
**You're right: I picked 10× to make the Tampa example work.** That's not a general rule.

The general question is *which place does the user most likely mean?* Standard geocoding services answer it with **population**: people usually mean the bigger city. Land area was only a stand-in because our Census places file has no population. Options:

| Rule | Problem |
|---|---|
| Always ask when the name matches more than one place | Almost every big city has small namesakes (Miami, OK; Houston, MO; Denver, PA; Phoenix, OR), so it would ask nearly every time |
| Largest land area by a factor of N | The N is arbitrary (your objection) |
| **Population, using a published threshold** ✅ | Needs one more Census file |

**Proposed rule:** a match counts as a **"major place"** if its population is **≥ 50,000**. That's the Census Bureau's own threshold for the core city of a metropolitan area, not a number I picked.
- **Exactly one major match → use it:** Tampa → Tampa, FL.
- **Two or more major matches → ask:** Springfield (IL, MO, MA, OR, OH), Portland (OR or ME), Kansas City (MO or KS), Columbus (OH, our hub, or GA). Asking is correct in these cases.
- **No major match:** pick the most populous if it's the only match, otherwise ask.
- **A state given by the user, or by the agent from the conversation** (e.g. "our Florida expansion"), always wins.

**Cost:** one more public Census file (city and town population estimates), about 20 minutes, and I'll check that it's available before using it.

## Updated choices
| # | Choice | Was | Now proposed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | Composite weights | .25/.20/.20/.20/.15 | **Equal 0.2**, plus a weight sensitivity test and analyst-set weights |
| 8 | Ambiguous names | 10× land area | **Census population ≥ 50,000 rule** (above) |
| 10 | Station rule | Precipitation + temperature | **+ gusts ≥ 90%**, with the fallback above |

Choices 1–5, 7 and 9 are unchanged.

content.text:
The better approach is to **stop weighting abstract scores and measure everything in one unit: expected disruption days per year.** The "weights" then come from the data, because a hazard that disrupts a hub more often contributes more days.

## Why weights were needed in the first place
The current design converts each hazard to a 0–100 score and then needs weights to combine them. Those scores have no shared meaning: 70 on winter and 70 on hurricanes aren't comparable, so *someone* has to decide how much each counts. That's where both my judgment-based weights and the equal weights came from.

## The alternative: count disruption days per hazard
For each hub and hazard, the data tells us **how many days per year it's likely to be disrupted**:

| Hazard | A "disruption day" is… | Data |
|---|---|---|
| Winter | Snow ≥ 5 cm, or observed glaze / freezing rain / ice pellets | Station, 1996–2025 |
| Flood | Rain ≥ 50 mm | Station, 1996–2025 |
| Convective | Gust ≥ 93 km/h, or a damaging tornado (EF1+) within 50 km | Station + SPC, 1996–2025 |
| Heat | High ≥ 38 °C | Station, 1996–2025 |
| Hurricane | A day when a storm of tropical-storm strength or more was within 150 km | HURDAT2, 1950–2025 |

**The overall KPI = expected disruption days per year, summed across hazards.**

### Why this is better
- **No subjective weights.** A hazard's share of the total *is* its share of disruption days, which is exactly the "some hazards are more likely to disrupt a hub" point you raised.
- **Severity is handled in the same unit.** A hurricane typically affects a hub for more than one day, and HURDAT2's 6-hourly positions tell us *how many* days each storm was within range. So multi-day events count as multiple days, measured from the data rather than assumed.
- **It's understandable for the business:** *"Dallas averages about 9 disruption days a year; ice and convective storms account for about 70% of them."* That reads better than "Dallas scores 63."
- **It reuses what we built.** The thresholds are the ones you've already reviewed, and the rare-event rates and uncertainty ranges carry over directly.

### Remaining assumptions, stated honestly
1. **Every disruption day counts the same**, whether it's a hurricane day or a heat day. That's still an assumption, but a far weaker and more visible one than five made-up weights. For a real client, it's the single input to ask for: *"What does a closure day cost you, by hazard?"* The agent can take those costs as an optional input, e.g. *"weight hurricane days 3×"*, and the result stays deterministic.
2. **Days are summed, so a day with two hazards counts twice.** For 1996–2025, where we have daily dates, we can measure how often that happens and report it. It's probably small.
3. **"Disruption" is defined by thresholds**, such as 5 cm of snow. A threshold is still a choice, but it comes with a stated reason and is applied the same way to every hub.

### What happens to FEMA's data
It becomes a **cross-check** and the source of **context** (e.g. FEMA's long-term winter or flood frequency for the county), not a score input. That also simplifies the design: one unit, measured at the hub.

### How this changes the earlier choices
| # | Was | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Scale inputs to 0–100 | **Not needed for the composite.** Per-hazard days are shown directly |
| 5 | 50/50 station vs FEMA within each hazard | **Replaced:** each hazard is defined by its disruption-day rule above; FEMA is a cross-check |
| 6 | Composite weights | **Replaced:** the sum of expected disruption days (optional cost-per-day input) |
| 7 | Tiers by thirds | Still thirds, now ranked by disruption days per year |
| New | — | Report how often hazards overlap on the same day |

The 0–100 sub-scores can still exist for **display**, e.g. "Dallas is in the top 10% for ice days," but no ranking depends on them.

Should I adopt this disruption-days approach, together with choices #8 (population rule) and #10 (gust requirement), and then start building?

"""SQLite connection and schema.

SQLite is the single store for this project: ~50 hubs x 10 years of daily weather
(~165k rows), FEMA NRI for all ~3.2k US counties, and Census place/county centroids.
"""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from app.config import get_settings

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hubs (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    region        TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    county_name   TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS daily_weather (
    hub_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES hubs(id),
    date           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- ISO date, local time of the hub
    tmax_c         REAL,
    tmin_c         REAL,
    precip_mm      REAL,
    snowfall_cm    REAL,
    wind_gust_kmh  REAL,
    weather_code   INTEGER,                -- WMO code (56/57/66/67 = freezing drizzle/rain)
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, date)
);

-- FEMA National Risk Index, one row per county x hazard, for ALL US counties.
-- freq_pctl (national percentile of annualized event frequency) is what scoring uses;
-- risk_score is kept for reference only (it scales with exposed property/population).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nri_county (
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard        TEXT NOT NULL,
    afreq         REAL,                    -- annualized frequency (events/year), NULL -> not applicable
    freq_pctl     REAL NOT NULL,           -- 0-100, national percentile of afreq (NULL treated as 0)
    alr_npctl     REAL,                    -- expected annual loss rate, national percentile
    risk_score    REAL,                    -- hazard type risk index score (exposure-driven)
    risk_rating   TEXT,
    nri_version   TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (county_fips, hazard)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS counties (
    county_fips   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS places (
    geoid         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa" (Census suffix like "city" removed)
    full_name     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa city"
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    aland_sqmi    REAL,                    -- land area; used to prefer the major place among same-name matches
    county_fips   TEXT                     -- nearest county centroid in the same state (approximation)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_places_name ON places(name);

-- NOAA HURDAT2 best tracks (Atlantic + NE Pacific), 6-hourly fixes, 1950+.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS storm_tracks (
    storm_id    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- e.g. AL092017
    name        TEXT,
    dt          TEXT NOT NULL,             -- ISO datetime (UTC)
    status      TEXT,                      -- TS, HU, SS, TD, EX, ...
    lat         REAL NOT NULL,
    lon         REAL NOT NULL,
    wind_kt     REAL,                      -- max sustained wind
    PRIMARY KEY (storm_id, dt)
);

-- NOAA SPC severe reports meeting the magnitude thresholds, kept only within the largest
-- tested radius of any hub (full national files stay cached in data/raw).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS severe_reports (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hazard      TEXT NOT NULL,             -- tornado | hail | wind
    date        TEXT NOT NULL,             -- local date of the report
    slat        REAL NOT NULL,
    slon        REAL NOT NULL,
    elat        REAL,                      -- tornado end point (NULL if unknown)
    elon        REAL,
    magnitude   REAL                       -- EF scale | hail inches | wind knots
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reports_hazard ON severe_reports(hazard, date);

-- Per-hub long-term event rates (Tier A), one row per hub x hazard x radius.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_event_rates (
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard          TEXT NOT NULL,         -- hurricane | hurricane_strength | tornado | hail | wind
    radius_km       REAL NOT NULL,
    first_year      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_year       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    events          INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- storms (hurricanes) or report days (convective)
    rate_per_year   REAL NOT NULL,
    rate_lo         REAL NOT NULL,         -- exact Poisson interval (confidence_level)
    rate_hi         REAL NOT NULL,
    p_horizon       REAL NOT NULL,         -- P(>= 1 event within horizon_years)
    horizon_years   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    params_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT,                  -- e.g. notable storms
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, hazard, radius_km)
);

-- Tier B: the GHCN-Daily station chosen for each hub by the fixed selection rule.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_stations (
    hub_id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    station_name    TEXT,
    lat             REAL, lon REAL,
    distance_km     REAL NOT NULL,
    completeness_json TEXT NOT NULL,       -- per element share of days present, 1996-2025
    candidates_tried INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS station_daily (
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    date            TEXT NOT NULL,
    prcp_mm         REAL,
    snow_cm         REAL,                  -- measured snowfall
    tmax_c          REAL,
    tmin_c          REAL,
    gust_kmh        REAL,                  -- WSF5: fastest 5-second wind
    wt_thunder      INTEGER,               -- WT03 observed (1) / not recorded (0)
    wt_ice_pellets  INTEGER,               -- WT04
    wt_hail         INTEGER,               -- WT05
    wt_glaze        INTEGER,               -- WT06
    wt_freezing_rain INTEGER,              -- WT17
    PRIMARY KEY (station_id, date)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_metrics (
    hub_id        TEXT NOT NULL,
    metric        TEXT NOT NULL,
    period        TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "2016-2025" or "2025"
    value         REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, metric, period)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS risk_scores (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    computed_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
    scoring_version TEXT NOT NULL,
    composite       REAL NOT NULL,
    winter          REAL, hurricane REAL, flood REAL, convective REAL, heat REAL,
    tier            TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scores_hub ON risk_scores(hub_id, computed_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
    old_value   REAL,
    new_value   REAL,
    message     TEXT NOT NULL,
    delivered   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ingest_log (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    source      TEXT NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    params      TEXT,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL,
    rows        INTEGER,
    note        TEXT
);
"""


def get_connection(db_file: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = db_file or get_settings().db_file
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=120)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn


def create_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    conn.commit()

# Method parameters (versioned). Data values are never altered; these settings only
# control how we compute from the data. Each has a rationale; see PLAN.md section 2.5.
# Same data + same params -> same output.

params_version: "1.1"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier A: long-term event records counted around each hub
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
event_rates:
  # Radius test: rates are computed for every radius; the middle one is the default
  # if hub rankings are stable across radii (checked by app.scoring.event_rates --test).
  radii_km:
    convective: [25, 50, 100]     # tornado / hail / wind
    hurricane: [100, 150, 200]
  default_radius_km:
    convective: 50                # metro-scale area; small enough to stay in one climate zone
    hurricane: 150                # damaging wind/rain extend far beyond a hurricane's center

  hurricane:
    source_files:                 # pinned NOAA NHC HURDAT2 releases (reproducible)
      - https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-1851-2025-092326.txt        # Atlantic
      - https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/hurdat/hurdat2-nepac-1949-2025-092926.txt  # NE Pacific
    first_year: 1950              # records reliable from aircraft reconnaissance onward
    last_year: 2025
    min_wind_kt: 34               # tropical-storm strength at closest approach
    hurricane_wind_kt: 64         # hurricane strength at closest approach (reported separately)
    statuses: [TS, HU, SS]        # tropical / subtropical storm, hurricane
    interpolate_step_km: 10       # densify the 6-hourly track before measuring distances

  convective:
    source_files:                 # pinned NOAA SPC severe-weather database files
      tornado: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/data/1950-2025_actual_tornadoes.csv
      hail: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/data/1955-2025_hail.csv.zip
      wind: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/data/1955-2025_wind.csv.zip
    first_year: 1996              # limits the long-term growth in reporting
    last_year: 2025
    min_magnitude:                # official severe thresholds / damaging tornadoes
      tornado: 1                  # EF1+ (EF0 reporting grew mostly with more observers)
      hail: 1.0                   # inches
      wind: 50                    # knots
    count_unit: report_days       # distinct days with >= 1 qualifying report within the radius

  probability_horizon_years: 10   # P(at least one event in N years) for investment decisions
  confidence_level: 0.90          # exact Poisson interval on the annual rate

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tier B: measured station data (NOAA GHCN-Daily)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
stations:
  stations_url: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/ghcnd-stations.txt
  inventory_url: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/ghcn/daily/ghcnd-inventory.txt
  data_url: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1
  station_prefix: USW             # US first-order (major airport / NWS) stations
  max_distance_km: 40
  first_year: 1996                # 30-year window, close to the climate-normal convention
  last_year: 2025
  # Must be >= min_completeness over the window. WSF5 (peak gust) is required so the rule
  # picks full-instrument (ASOS) stations, which also report weather events; event flags
  # themselves can't be completeness-checked because they only appear on event days.
  required_elements: [PRCP, TMAX, WSF5]
  # If no station within range has gusts, take the nearest with these and flag the hub
  # as having no measured gusts (Open-Meteo modeled gusts are used instead).
  fallback_required_elements: [PRCP, TMAX]
  min_completeness: 0.90
  elements: [PRCP, SNOW, TMAX, TMIN, WSF5, WT03, WT04, WT05, WT06, WT17]
  # WT03 thunder, WT04 ice pellets/sleet, WT05 hail, WT06 glaze/rime, WT17 freezing rain

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring: expected disruption days per year (no subjective hazard weights)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
scoring:
  scoring_version: "2.0"
  window: [1996, 2025]            # station-based hazards; hurricanes use event_rates.hurricane years
  # A variable whose station data covers < min_coverage of the window (after filling 2016+
  # gaps from Open-Meteo) is computed from Open-Meteo 2016-2025 instead, and flagged.
  min_coverage: 0.80

  # A hub-day counts as disrupted by a hazard when its rule is met.
  disruption_rules:
    winter: "snow >= 5 cm, or observed glaze / freezing rain / ice pellets"
    flood: "precipitation >= 50 mm"
    convective: "measured gust >= 93 km/h (58 mph, the NWS severe-wind level), or an EF1+ tornado within 50 km"
    heat: "daily high >= 38 C (100 F)"
    hurricane: "a tropical-storm-strength (34 kt+) storm within 150 km at any time that day"
  thresholds:
    disruption_snow_cm: 5
    disruption_precip_mm: 50
    disruption_gust_kmh: 93
    disruption_heat_c: 38
  # Optional cost per disruption day by hazard (all 1 = every disruption day counts the same).
  # A client can supply real costs; the composite then becomes expected cost-weighted days.
  default_day_costs: {winter: 1, flood: 1, convective: 1, hurricane: 1, heat: 1}

  # Descriptive metrics (shown in answers, not used for ranking).
  descriptive_thresholds:
    snow_day_cm: 1.0
    trace_snow_cm: 0.1
    heavy_snow_cm: 10
    extreme_cold_c: -15
    heavy_rain_mm: 50
    extreme_heat_c: 38
    damaging_gust_kmh: 93

  tiers: thirds                   # top / middle / bottom third of hubs by composite days

  confidence_rules:               # each true condition lowers confidence one level (high -> medium -> low)
    station_far_km: 25
    gust_not_measured: true
    variable_from_open_meteo: true  # any scored variable fell back to Open-Meteo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stand-in hubs for places that aren't hubs (find_nearest_hubs)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
stand_in:
  candidates: 3
  w_similarity: 0.8
  w_proximity: 0.2
  proximity_zero_km: 500          # proximity score falls linearly from 100 at 0 km to 0 here
  far_caveat_km: 250
  # Hazard profile = FEMA NRI annualized frequency for these hazards, each scaled by the
  # 95th percentile across all US counties (capped at 1) so the 10 hazards are comparable.
  profile_hazards: [winter_weather, ice_storm, cold_wave, hurricane, coastal_flood,
                    inland_flood, tornado, hail, strong_wind, heat_wave]
  profile_scale_percentile: 95
  # Ambiguous place names: a "major place" has population >= this (the Census Bureau's
  # population threshold for a metropolitan area's core). Exactly one major match -> use it.
  major_place_population: 50000
  fuzzy_cutoff: 0.85

# population threshold for a metropolitan area's core). Exactly one major match -> use it.

from pathlib import Path

from app.config import get_settings

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hubs (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    region        TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    county_name   TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS daily_weather (
    hub_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES hubs(id),
    date           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- ISO date, local time of the hub
    tmax_c         REAL,
    tmin_c         REAL,
    precip_mm      REAL,
    snowfall_cm    REAL,
    wind_gust_kmh  REAL,
    weather_code   INTEGER,                -- WMO code (56/57/66/67 = freezing drizzle/rain)
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, date)
);

-- FEMA National Risk Index, one row per county x hazard, for ALL US counties.
-- freq_pctl (national percentile of annualized event frequency) is what scoring uses;
-- risk_score is kept for reference only (it scales with exposed property/population).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nri_county (
    county_fips   TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard        TEXT NOT NULL,
    afreq         REAL,                    -- annualized frequency (events/year), NULL -> not applicable
    freq_pctl     REAL NOT NULL,           -- 0-100, national percentile of afreq (NULL treated as 0)
    alr_npctl     REAL,                    -- expected annual loss rate, national percentile
    risk_score    REAL,                    -- hazard type risk index score (exposure-driven)
    risk_rating   TEXT,
    nri_version   TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (county_fips, hazard)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS counties (
    county_fips   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS places (
    geoid         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa" (Census suffix like "city" removed)
    full_name     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "Tampa city"
    state         TEXT NOT NULL,
    lat           REAL NOT NULL,
    lon           REAL NOT NULL,
    aland_sqmi    REAL,                    -- land area; used to prefer the major place among same-name matches
    county_fips   TEXT                     -- nearest county centroid in the same state (approximation)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_places_name ON places(name);

-- NOAA HURDAT2 best tracks (Atlantic + NE Pacific), 6-hourly fixes, 1950+.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS storm_tracks (
    storm_id    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- e.g. AL092017
    name        TEXT,
    dt          TEXT NOT NULL,             -- ISO datetime (UTC)
    status      TEXT,                      -- TS, HU, SS, TD, EX, ...
    lat         REAL NOT NULL,
    lon         REAL NOT NULL,
    wind_kt     REAL,                      -- max sustained wind
    PRIMARY KEY (storm_id, dt)
);

-- NOAA SPC severe reports meeting the magnitude thresholds, kept only within the largest
-- tested radius of any hub (full national files stay cached in data/raw).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS severe_reports (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hazard      TEXT NOT NULL,             -- tornado | hail | wind
    date        TEXT NOT NULL,             -- local date of the report
    slat        REAL NOT NULL,
    slon        REAL NOT NULL,
    elat        REAL,                      -- tornado end point (NULL if unknown)
    elon        REAL,
    magnitude   REAL                       -- EF scale | hail inches | wind knots
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_reports_hazard ON severe_reports(hazard, date);

-- Per-hub long-term event rates (Tier A), one row per hub x hazard x radius.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_event_rates (
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    hazard          TEXT NOT NULL,         -- hurricane | hurricane_strength | tornado | hail | wind
    radius_km       REAL NOT NULL,
    first_year      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_year       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    events          INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- storms (hurricanes) or report days (convective)
    rate_per_year   REAL NOT NULL,
    rate_lo         REAL NOT NULL,         -- exact Poisson interval (confidence_level)
    rate_hi         REAL NOT NULL,
    p_horizon       REAL NOT NULL,         -- P(>= 1 event within horizon_years)
    horizon_years   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    params_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT,                  -- e.g. notable storms
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, hazard, radius_km)
);

-- Tier B: the GHCN-Daily station chosen for each hub by the fixed selection rule.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_stations (
    hub_id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    station_name    TEXT,
    lat             REAL, lon REAL,
    distance_km     REAL NOT NULL,
    completeness_json TEXT NOT NULL,       -- per element share of days present, 1996-2025
    candidates_tried INTEGER NOT NULL,
    gust_measured   INTEGER NOT NULL       -- 0 = fallback station without peak-gust data
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS station_daily (
    station_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    date            TEXT NOT NULL,
    prcp_mm         REAL,
    snow_cm         REAL,                  -- measured snowfall
    tmax_c          REAL,
    tmin_c          REAL,
    gust_kmh        REAL,                  -- WSF5: fastest 5-second wind
    wt_thunder      INTEGER,               -- WT03 observed (1) / not recorded (0)
    wt_ice_pellets  INTEGER,               -- WT04
    wt_hail         INTEGER,               -- WT05
    wt_glaze        INTEGER,               -- WT06
    wt_freezing_rain INTEGER,              -- WT17
    PRIMARY KEY (station_id, date)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hub_metrics (
    hub_id        TEXT NOT NULL,
    metric        TEXT NOT NULL,
    period        TEXT NOT NULL,           -- e.g. "2016-2025" or "2025"
    value         REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hub_id, metric, period)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS risk_scores (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    computed_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
    scoring_version TEXT NOT NULL,
    composite       REAL NOT NULL,
    winter          REAL, hurricane REAL, flood REAL, convective REAL, heat REAL,
    tier            TEXT NOT NULL,
    details_json    TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scores_hub ON risk_scores(hub_id, computed_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    hub_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
    old_value   REAL,
    new_value   REAL,
    message     TEXT NOT NULL,
    delivered   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ingest_log (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    source      TEXT NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    params      TEXT,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL,
    rows        INTEGER,
    note        TEXT
);
"""


def get_connection(db_file: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    path = db_file or get_settings().db_file
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=120)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn


def create_schema(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    conn.commit()

"""US Census Bureau Gazetteer files: every US place (city/town/CDP) and county centroid.

Used to locate places that are not hubs (e.g. "Tampa, FL") without any live API call.
A place's county is approximated as the nearest county centroid in the same state.
"""

import io
import re
import sqlite3
import zipfile

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import create_schema
from app.ingest.common import get_with_retry, http_client, log_ingest

YEAR = 2026
BASE = f"https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/gazetteer/{YEAR}_Gazetteer"
PLACES_URL = f"{BASE}/{YEAR}_Gaz_place_national.zip"
COUNTIES_URL = f"{BASE}/{YEAR}_Gaz_counties_national.zip"

# Census place-name suffixes ("Tampa city", "Brandon CDP") -> stripped for matching.
SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s+(city and borough|consolidated government \(balance\)|metropolitan government \(balance\)|"
    r"unified government \(balance\)|metro government \(balance\)|\(balance\)|city|town|village|"
    r"borough|CDP|municipality|comunidad|zona urbana|urban county|plantation|corporation)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _download_table(url: str, cache_name: str, refresh: bool) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cache = get_settings().raw_dir / cache_name
    if refresh or not cache.exists():
        with http_client() as c:
            content = get_with_retry(c, url).content
        cache.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cache.write_bytes(content)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(cache) as z:
        name = next(n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith(".txt"))
        raw = z.read(name).decode("latin-1")
    sep = "|" if raw.split("\n", 1)[0].count("|") > raw.split("\n", 1)[0].count("\t") else "\t"
    df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(raw), sep=sep, dtype=str)
    df.columns = [c.strip() for c in df.columns]
    return df


def clean_place_name(name: str) -> str:
    """'Tampa city' -> 'Tampa'; 'Nashville-Davidson metropolitan government (balance)' -> 'Nashville-Davidson'."""
    prev = None
    while prev != name:
        prev, name = name, SUFFIX_RE.sub("", name).strip()
    return name


def nearest_county(places: pd.DataFrame, counties: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """For each place, the nearest county centroid within the same state (equirectangular distance)."""
    out = pd.Series(index=places.index, dtype=object)
    for state, grp in places.groupby("state"):
        cs = counties[counties["state"] == state]
        if cs.empty:
            continue
        plat, plon = np.radians(grp["lat"].to_numpy())[:, None], np.radians(grp["lon"].to_numpy())[:, None]
        clat, clon = np.radians(cs["lat"].to_numpy())[None, :], np.radians(cs["lon"].to_numpy())[None, :]
        x = (clon - plon) * np.cos((plat + clat) / 2)
        y = clat - plat
        idx = np.argmin(x * x + y * y, axis=1)
        out.loc[grp.index] = cs["county_fips"].to_numpy()[idx]
    return out


def ingest(conn: sqlite3.Connection, refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
    cdf = _download_table(COUNTIES_URL, f"{YEAR}_Gaz_counties_national.zip", refresh)
    counties = pd.DataFrame({
        "county_fips": cdf["GEOID"].str.zfill(5),
        "name": cdf["NAME"],
        "state": cdf["USPS"],
        "lat": cdf["INTPTLAT"].astype(float),
        "lon": cdf["INTPTLONG"].astype(float),
    })

    pdf = _download_table(PLACES_URL, f"{YEAR}_Gaz_place_national.zip", refresh)
    places = pd.DataFrame({
        "geoid": pdf["GEOID"],
        "full_name": pdf["NAME"],
        "state": pdf["USPS"],
        "lat": pdf["INTPTLAT"].astype(float),
        "lon": pdf["INTPTLONG"].astype(float),
        "aland_sqmi": pd.to_numeric(pdf["ALAND_SQMI"], errors="coerce"),
    })
    places["name"] = places["full_name"].map(clean_place_name)
    places["county_fips"] = nearest_county(places, counties)

    conn.execute("DELETE FROM counties")
    # Recreate places so schema changes (new columns) apply to existing databases.
    conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS places")
    create_schema(conn)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO counties VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", counties.itertuples(index=False))
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT INTO places (geoid, name, full_name, state, lat, lon, aland_sqmi, county_fips) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
        [tuple(None if pd.isna(v) else v for v in row) for row in
         places[["geoid", "name", "full_name", "state", "lat", "lon", "aland_sqmi", "county_fips"]]
         .itertuples(index=False)],
    )
    conn.commit()
    log_ingest(conn, "census_gazetteer", "ok", rows=len(places) + len(counties),
               params={"year": YEAR}, note=f"places={len(places)}, counties={len(counties)}")
    return {"places": len(places), "counties": len(counties)}

import pandas as pd

SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s+(city and borough|consolidated government \(balance\)|metropolitan government \(balance\)|"
    r"unified government \(balance\)|metro government \(balance\)|\(balance\)|city|town|village|"
    r"borough|CDP|municipality|comunidad|zona urbana|urban county|plantation|corporation)$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _download_table(url: str, cache_name: str, refresh: bool) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cache = get_settings().raw_dir / cache_name
    if refresh or not cache.exists():
        with http_client() as c:
            content = get_with_retry(c, url).content
        cache.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cache.write_bytes(content)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(cache) as z:
        name = next(n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith(".txt"))
        raw = z.read(name).decode("latin-1")
    sep = "|" if raw.split("\n", 1)[0].count("|") > raw.split("\n", 1)[0].count("\t") else "\t"
    df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(raw), sep=sep, dtype=str)
    df.columns = [c.strip() for c in df.columns]
    return df


def clean_place_name(name: str) -> str:
    """'Tampa city' -> 'Tampa'; 'Nashville-Davidson metropolitan government (balance)' -> 'Nashville-Davidson'."""
    prev = None

    """For each place, the nearest county centroid within the same state (equirectangular distance)."""
